Position Summary Bristol Myers Squibb is seeking a manager to advance data governance and data quality within PDS, helping business functions manage and use data as a trusted, reusable business asset. The role engages business and functional stakeholders, process owners, data owners and stewards to understand business needs and build alignment on governance initiatives, data standards, ownership, quality expectations and measurable outcomes. Working with data engineering and technology teams, the Manager translates agreed priorities into actionable requirements, coordinates data-quality issue resolution and supports the delivery and adoption of governed data products and analytics using Databricks and enterprise data lakes. The Manager communicates the business value of well-governed, high-quality data and helps users apply reliable insights in operational decisions. The Manager owns assigned workstreams and deliverables, with strategic direction and prioritization provided by the Senior Manager or Data Domain Lead. Key Responsibilities – Data Quality and Governance · Work with data owners and stewards to document critical data elements, definitions, ownership, data-quality rules and acceptance thresholds. · Support metadata, lineage, access, privacy and data-quality controls required for governed and fit-for-purpose data products. · Investigate data issues with business and technical teams; document root cause, resolution and prevention actions. · Promote consistent governance practices across data lake, Databricks and downstream data-product delivery. Business Analysis and Adoption · Analyze operational pain points and translate them into prioritized data-product backlog items. · Prepare demonstrations, user guidance, training materials and adoption communications. · Collect user feedback and product measures to support continuous improvement. · Help users discover available data, understand product definitions and apply data consistently in business decisions. Data Platform and Product Execution Support end-to-end delivery of data products and analytics for an assigned PDS domain or use case, from discovery and requirements through testing, release and adoption. Work with data engineering teams to use enterprise data lake and Databricks capabilities for data ingestion, transformation, curation and consumption. Gather and document business requirements, data definitions, user stories, acceptance criteria, source-to-target needs and process impacts. Help define reusable data products with clear consumers, business value, ownership, service expectations and measurable success criteria. Coordinate working sessions with business experts, data stewards, data engineers and technology teams. Track actions, risks, dependencies, decisions and delivery milestones; escalate issues promptly. Collaboration and Ways of Working · Engage business and functional stakeholders, process owners, data owners and stewards to understand business needs, communicate the value of data governance and data quality, and build alignment on priorities, ownership and expected outcomes. · Facilitate cross-functional discussions to agree on data standards, data-quality expectations and remediation priorities; coordinate with business and technology teams to implement agreed actions and drive adoption of data governance initiatives. · Contribute to a practical, inclusive and data-driven culture within PDS. Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Representative opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation. About the role: We are looking for a SOC Engineer to join our Security Operations team and help defend a fast-moving, cloud-native AI vibe-coding platform. In this role, your primary mandate will be building and evolving our security data lake, engineering reliable security telemetry, and owning high-fidelity detection engineering end-to-end. You will unify cloud, identity, endpoint, and application telemetry, staying on top of emerging threats to rapidly build and tune detections across our environment. Alongside this data and detection mandate, you will support incident investigations as needed to translate real-world threats into stronger automated defenses. This is a hands-on engineering role requiring strong technical depth, understanding of modern software engineering and CI/CD systems, familiarity with cloud-native infrastructure (especially GCP), and expertise in security data pipelines and detection workflows. What You'll Do: - Security Data Lake & Detection Engineering: Architect, expand, and maintain our security data lake while designing, testing, and tuning custom detection rules to maximize threat coverage and minimize noise across our cloud-native stack. - Threat Awareness & Rapid Assessment: Continuously monitor emerging threats (0-days, bad actor activity, public exploitation campaigns, bug bounty reports, customer security issues) and rapidly assess their applicability to Replit's infrastructure, SaaS services, internal tools, and platform components. - Investigation & Impact Analysis: Conduct targeted investigations to determine impact, analyze logs, telemetry, and system behaviors using SIEM, metrics, and Cloud Logging and identify gaps in detection/visibility. Required Skills & Experience: - Building and evolving the security data lake, unifying cloud, identity, endpoint, and application telemetry; hands-on experience with SIEM, Cloud Logging, and log-based investigation workflows. - Engineering reliable security infrastructure and automation using infrastructure-as-code to close visibility gaps and perform log-based investigations. - Proven expertise in detection engineering end-to-end, specifically developing, testing, and tuning custom detection rules to maximize threat coverage and reduce noise across complex environments. - Strong understanding of software engineering fundamentals (code structure, build systems, dependencies, package ecosystems). - Understanding of CI/CD pipelines and DevOps workflows. - Solid knowledge of cloud architecture, especially Google Cloud Platform (GCP) services in modern cloud-native deployments. - Familiarity with SaaS architectures, identity systems, and integration patterns. Bonus Qualifications: - Experience with threat intelligence, security research, or vulnerability analysis. - Familiarity with Kubernetes, containers, serverless infrastructure, or modern distributed systems. - Ability to write scripts or small tools for investigation or automation (Python, Go, Bash). - Experience working with bug bounty programs or coordinated vulnerability disclosure workflows. - Experience in fast-paced, cloud-native, or AI/ML-driven environments. jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Claude Design lets anyone collaborate with Claude to create polished visual work: interactive prototypes, product mockups, slides, and animations. We're making Claude the best visual storyteller there is, lowering the floor so anyone can bring an idea to life, and raising the ceiling on what the most skilled creators can make. We work on Artifacts in Claude, and so far we've shipped new kinds of artifacts like Claude Design, Slides, and Motion, and we are exploring new bets. We're looking for Software Engineers to help build and shape Claude Design and the creative capabilities of Claude. This is a craft-heavy, product engineering role: you'll create the canvas, real-time editing, design-system inference, and AI-driven generation experiences that make AI-generated design feel like a tool people reach for first, not a demo. You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge research and real-world application, rapidly building and testing new experiences, partnering directly with researchers and users, and helping to generate the crucial insights that shape where the product goes next. You'll join a small, fast-moving team with high autonomy. If you're a strong design engineer who loves building visual products and likes to sweat the details, we'd love to hear from you. Key responsibilities Build and ship user-facing features across our products, and help decide which creative spaces we explore next Set technical direction for these products, including editor and canvas architecture, real-time collaboration, and rich import and export Own the quality bar for how these products look and feel, treating latency, responsiveness, and reliability as first-class concerns and raising user experience and design considerations early Partner with researchers to rapidly prototype experiences around vision and generation capabilities, and help improve the quality of what Claude generates Spend time with users and dig into how people actually use what you ship, then turn what you learn into what we build next Build the shared foundations that let us launch new creative tools quickly and make them work well together Minimum qualifications Strong design sensibility and a high bar for craft, including attention to interaction details, motion, and polish Strong full-stack engineering skills, including production frontend and backend work on user-facing web products Ability to thrive in ambiguity and be energized by uncertainty High agency, good judgment about what matters, and a bias toward shipping A deeply user-centric approach: you validate ideas with actual users before over-investing and talk about problems before solutions Strong opinions held loosely: you advocate forcefully for ideas but change your mind based on evidence Care for Anthropic's mission and the societal impacts of your work Preferred qualifications Extensive experience working with or building visual collaboration and creative tools Experience with UI and UX for AI-powered applications, and fluency collaborating closely with designers Deep frontend expertise in canvas rendering, complex editor UIs, design-system tooling, or graphics work, such as WebGL, shaders, 3D, or animation Experience with real-time, collaborative applications, such as multiplayer editing and WebSockets Background conducting user research, interviews, and usability testing Experience building and shipping products from 0 to 1 Experience building product platforms, primitives, or shared foundations that other products and teams build on top of Performance optimization experience, such as profiling, improving rendering, and tracing end-to-end latency The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $405,000 — $485,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

The team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform. About the Role We’re looking for an RTL Design Engineer to help design and develop next-generation AI accelerator silicon. In this role, you'll work across architecture, microarchitecture, and RTL implementation, translating complex system and performance requirements into efficient, scalable hardware designs. You'll collaborate closely with silicon architects, hardware and software engineers, verification, and physical design teams to co-design hardware solutions optimized for demanding AI workloads. This is a hands-on engineering role with opportunities to influence architectural decisions, drive microarchitecture development, and own RTL design from early concept through implementation and integration. We're particularly interested in engineers with experience in Network-on-Chip (NoC), networking, interconnect architectures, or high-performance data movement, though the role encompasses broader RTL design and hardware co-design challenges. In this role, you will: - Design and implement high-performance RTL for next-generation AI accelerator silicon, from microarchitecture definition through implementation and integration. - Collaborate with architecture and software teams to translate system-level requirements into efficient hardware microarchitectures. - Drive hardware/software co-design efforts to optimize performance, power, area, and scalability for AI workloads. - Develop and optimize RTL for complex datapaths, control logic, interconnects, and other critical silicon subsystems. - Evaluate architectural and microarchitectural tradeoffs across bandwidth, latency, throughput, and resource utilization. - Partner with design verification and formal verification teams to ensure functional correctness, develop verification strategies, and debug complex design issues. - Work closely with physical design teams to optimize RTL for synthesis, timing closure, power, and area. - Contribute to architecture reviews, design specifications, and cross-functional discussions to influence future silicon designs. - Support block-level and SoC-level integration, debugging, and performance optimization. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have strong hands-on experience with ASIC RTL design and microarchitecture development using SystemVerilog or Verilog. - Have experience designing and implementing complex digital hardware blocks, from architecture and specification through RTL development and verification. - Understand hardware architecture and microarchitecture tradeoffs, including performance, power, area, latency, and throughput. - Have experience collaborating across architecture, software, verification, and physical design teams to develop optimized hardware solutions. - Can reason about complex hardware systems, identify performance bottlenecks, and translate architectural requirements into efficient RTL implementations. - Have experience with synthesis, timing closure, and physical implementation considerations. - Enjoy working on ambiguous, technically challenging problems and taking ownership of designs from concept through integration. - Bring experience with Network-on-Chip (NoC), networking, interconnect fabrics, packet-based architectures, or high-bandwidth data movement systems. - Experience with AI accelerators, high-performance computing, or hardware/software co-design is a plus. To comply with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidates for this role may need to meet certain legal status requirements as provided in those laws and regulations. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. jobs.title: Staff Product Designer, DashPass — Affordability & New Benefits
jobs.description: About the role We're looking for a Staff Product Designer to shape how DashPass delivers more value through affordability and new benefits. You'll join the Affordability pod within New Benefits, turning emerging customer needs into experiences that make everyday purchases more accessible and membership more valuable. This is a hands-on role with room to define the problem, set direction, and build. You'll work directly with product, engineering, research, analytics, and business partners to identify opportunities, test new concepts, and bring them to market. You'll connect a longer-term vision to the next experiment, staying close to the interaction, visual, and implementation details that make an experience feel simple and considered. We're building a team of designers who combine deep craft with the ability to bring ideas to life. You'll use AI throughout your workflow to explore possibilities, build working prototypes, and shorten the path from an idea to a shipped experience. Your judgment will shape both what we build and how the team builds it. You're excited about this opportunity because you will… Set direction in an emerging space. Turn customer insights, business goals, and incomplete inputs into a clear point of view, product briefs, and a sequence of experiments and launches. Influence what gets built. Build alignment with product and engineering leaders, shape priorities across the pod and adjacent teams, and resolve tradeoffs between customer value, feasibility, and business impact. Own the work from concept through launch. Move between problem framing, exploration, prototyping, and implementation, taking initiative to close gaps and keep the work moving. Deliver a high bar for craft. Create intuitive flows, precise visual design, and thoughtful interactions that make benefits and savings easy to understand and use, with accessibility and consistency built in. Build with AI. Use AI-assisted design and coding to make realistic prototypes, test ideas with customers, and contribute product improvements alongside engineers. Create reusable tools and workflows that help teammates move faster while preserving quality. Ship, learn, and improve. Partner with research and analytics to define success, evaluate experiments, and improve experiences based on customer understanding, benefit adoption, and membership engagement. Multiply the team's impact. Coach designers on craft and product thinking, share effective AI workflows, and strengthen shared patterns and hiring practices that raise the team's quality bar. We're excited about you because… Your body of shipped work demonstrates refined visual and interaction design, thoughtful systems thinking, and attention to the details of the final product. You've taken ambiguous opportunities from problem definition to launch, shaping what a team built and demonstrating what changed for customers and the business. You establish priorities and make progress with limited direction, identifying missing inputs, bringing the right partners together, and making decisions as new evidence emerges. You've influenced roadmaps and earned alignment across product, engineering, and business partners through clear reasoning, customer evidence, and tangible prototypes. AI is already part of how you work. You can show working prototypes, product changes, or reusable tools you've built with AI, explain your own contribution, and evaluate the quality of the output. You work directly with engineers on implementation, understand technical constraints, and use code to explore and refine an experience. You know when to explore broadly and when to narrow scope, balancing speed, craft, and customer value. You strengthen the work around you through critique, coaching, and shared practices. Experience with consumer subscriptions, marketplaces, pricing, savings, or benefits is a plus. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future. In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others. To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here . See below for paid time off details: For salaried roles: flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year. jobs.title: Associate Clinical Oncology Specialist
jobs.description: Territiory: West Broward, FL The Associate Clinical Oncology Specialist (ACOS) is responsible for contributing to account sales, service, and support activities of all Oncology products. The role includes ensuring patients adherence to the prescribed test cadence with a focus on improving patient outcomes. The individual will identify areas of improvement in clinical workflows, test fulfillment, internal systems and processes. Responsibilities include cultivating and maintaining key relationships and working with customers and internal partners that enable Signatera patient retention and unit growth within existing customers. Primary Responsibilities: Work with assigned COS to grow, maintain & support existing customers Build relationships with key personnel at assigned Oncology accounts to facilitate unit growth. Analyze and monitor patient testing to ensure that patients remain on the protocol prescribed by the Oncologist. Assess the needs of medical professionals and staff members with a focus on customer support, coordination of logistics, and problem solving Become experts on all Natera Oncology products and processes to maximize effectiveness in the field. Educate medical professionals on the tools and resources that Natera provides to facilitate test order management Utilize and maintain internal reports of key performance indicators (KPIs) related to patient retention and fulfilled order volume. Be a key team player within the sales organization who can partner with internal stakeholders, such as sales reps, patient coordinators, territory managers, etc., to achieve the best outcomes for the patient and the provider. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree preferred or Associate’s degree with minimum of 3 years of relevant experience Medical assistant, clinical support, patient liaison or nursing background in oncology or a Minimum of 2 years of medical sales experience Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: Thrives in ambiguous environments Exceptionally bright, flexible, self-motivated, and results oriented with strong interpersonal and analytical skills Ability to think strategically as well as execute tactically Must act with a sense of urgency Have a strong desire to work in a fast-pace environment and must work independently with an internal drive to be successful Excellent organizational and communication skills (written and verbal) with demonstrated ability to effectively present to both internal and external customers Effective time management skills required with a demonstrated ability to assess and prioritize Proficient in Microsoft PowerPoint and Excel; Gmail Fluent in understanding data spreadsheets and technologies, although the Patient Retention Specialists will continue to lead patient identification and vetting Demonstrated ability to quickly learn software and reporting systems Physical Demands & Work Environment: Duties are typically performed in a medical office or hospital setting. This position requires the ability to use a computer keyboard, communicate over the telephone and read printed material. Duties may require working outside normal working hours (evenings and weekends) at times. 25-50% travel required In addition to a base salary, we offer uncapped commission, a car allowance program, and Restricted Stock Units (RSUs). The compensation package listed is for 1st year OTE, which are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. On-target earnings (OTE) represent the total potential income an employee can earn by achieving 100% of their performance goals. It combines a base salary with commissions and serves as an estimated figure rather than a guaranteed amount, providing a guideline based on average performance outcomes. On-target earnings (OTE) $110,000 — $130,000 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! cold_email.subject: Interest in Associate Clinical Oncology Specialist — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate Clinical Oncology Specialist opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

Position Summary The Senior Manager Electrical Engineer, Site Infrastructure (Principle Engineer) serves as a technical owner and subject-matter expert for the site's critical electrical infrastructure. This individual will own and advance medium-voltage and high-power distribution, electrical system automation and controls, electrical system reliability, capital projects, commissioning, troubleshooting, and long-term infrastructure planning for a large-scale, continuously operating manufacturing campus. We welcome candidates from biopharmaceutical manufacturing as well as adjacent industries such as semiconductor fabrication, data centers, utilities, advanced manufacturing, energy, and engineering or construction services. Direct GMP experience is helpful but not required. Candidates with strong critical-power and industrial electrical experience will be supported in learning the applicable regulated manufacturing requirements. This is an onsite technical leadership role that is currently an individual-contributor position, with significant system ownership and cross-functional influence. The role may evolve in the future to include a reporting engineering team. The role is well suited for an engineer who wants to own systems through their full lifecycle, lead meaningful infrastructure investments, apply high-power and electrical automation expertise to critical systems, and support reliable operations connected to the delivery of medicines to patients. Duties/Responsibilities Serve as the technical owner and electrical engineering subject-matter expert for assigned site infrastructure and utility systems. Provide engineering oversight for medium-voltage and high-power distribution, power infrastructure, electrical equipment, emergency systems, and associated site utilities. Lead the specification, integration, and lifecycle management of electrical system automation, controls, and monitoring (for example, power monitoring, supervisory control, and protection and metering systems) in coordination with controls and automation partners. Lead or support electrical projects from concept and scope development through design, construction, commissioning, startup, and operational handover. Develop and review technical requirements, specifications, drawings, equipment selections, and engineering documentation. Perform or oversee power-system studies, such as short-circuit, protective-device coordination, arc-flash, and load-flow analysis, to support safe and reliable operation and system changes. Troubleshoot complex electrical-system issues and partner with operations and maintenance teams to improve reliability and reduce downtime. Coordinate with internal stakeholders, engineering partners, contractors, equipment suppliers, and the local electrical utility provider. Support infrastructure planning, system-capacity assessments, equipment lifecycle strategies, and capital-investment recommendations. Provide electrical engineering support for site changes, investigations, inspections, and compliance activities. Review commissioning documents, system turnover packages, as-built drawings, preventive-maintenance requirements, and operating procedures. Promote effective collaboration and ensure engineering work is completed safely, reliably, and in alignment with site priorities. Provide technical direction and mentorship to project teams and peers. This role does not currently have direct reports but may include leading an engineering team in the future. Support a continuously operating facility, including participation in the established escalation or on-call model and occasional off-hours support for critical events, planned shutdowns, and major project activities. Qualifications Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a closely related engineering discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant technical experience. Demonstrated technical leadership, including mentoring engineers and directing technical work across project teams, vendors, and contractors. At least 8 years of electrical engineering experience supporting large-scale industrial, manufacturing, utility, or critical-infrastructure operations. Hands-on experience with medium-voltage or high-voltage electrical distribution systems, including power distribution, switchgear, substations, transformers, protection systems, emergency power, or related infrastructure. Experience with electrical system automation, controls, or monitoring (for example, power monitoring, supervisory control, or protective-relay communications) for power distribution and electrical infrastructure. Working knowledge of applicable electrical codes and standards (for example, NFPA 70, NFPA 70E, and IEEE standards) and of power-system analysis, including short-circuit, protective-device coordination, and arc-flash studies. Experience serving as a technical lead, system owner, project engineer, or subject-matter expert for electrical systems. Experience troubleshooting electrical systems and supporting equipment reliability in an operating facility. Experience developing technical scopes, specifications, user requirements, or design requirements for electrical infrastructure projects. Experience supporting projects through design, installation, commissioning, startup, and operational handover. Ability to read and interpret single-line diagrams, electrical drawings, equipment specifications, and technical documentation. Ability to coordinate across operations, maintenance, engineering, safety, vendors, contractors, and other technical stakeholders. Ability to manage multiple technical priorities and provide support for a continuously operating site, including occasional off-hours support for significant electrical issues or planned project activities. Preferred Qualifications Experience in biopharmaceutical, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, data center, utility, chemical, energy, or advanced-manufacturing environments. Experience working in a regulated or highly controlled operating environment. Experience leading, coaching, and developing engineers, including work prioritization, performance feedback, and team development, as the role may include direct reports in the future. Familiarity with GMP, commissioning, qualification, validation, change control, deviation, or CAPA processes. Experience with 13.8 kV electrical distribution or comparable medium-voltage infrastructure. Experience with fire-alarm, fire-suppression, emergency-power, or building utility systems. Experience with power-system analysis software (for example, ETAP or SKM) or 3D plant-design or engineering-modeling software. Professional Engineer license. You may be a strong fit if... Prior pharmaceutical experience is not required if you bring strong experience in critical power, high-power and medium-voltage distribution, electrical system automation, system ownership, commissioning, reliability, and continuously operating facilities. cold_email.subject: Interest in Principle Electrical Engineer — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Bristol Myers Squibb Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Principle Electrical Engineer opportunity with Bristol Myers Squibb at Bristol Myers Squibb.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Beneficial Deployments
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the Role: At Anthropic, we're building AI systems that are safe, beneficial, and transformative. Our mission is to develop AI that benefits humanity, and we believe the most powerful capabilities emerge when we thoughtfully bridge the gap between research breakthroughs and real-world applications. Many of the people who could gain the most from Claude are the least able to buy it the usual way. A teacher often pays for tools out of pocket. A small nonprofit has no procurement team. A university lab that wants to use Claude has to go through funding, an IT office, and a purchasing department at once. Beneficial Deployments works to reach them, through programs like Claude for Teachers and Claude for Nonprofits and through our work with researchers. What stands between those people and Claude is rarely the model. It's proving they qualify, getting the right price, buying in a way their institution allows, and landing in the right organization with the right permissions. Those steps run through identity, billing, provisioning, and fraud systems that were built for commercial customers. Our Access team makes them work for everyone else. We're looking for engineers who find it deeply satisfying to remove the one thing stopping thousands of teachers or scientists from getting started. You'll work in other teams' codebases as often as our own, and much of the job is earning the trust of the engineers, accountants, and safety reviewers who own those systems. This role's focus is access. Experience with billing or identity is a big plus. What matters most is that you finish hard things that cross team lines, get the details right when money and trust are involved, and care about who is on the other end. Core Responsibilities: Own programs like Claude for Teachers or Claude for Nonprofits from design through launch, operation, and support Support the verification lifecycle: how educators, nonprofits, and research labs prove eligibility, get reviewed at scale, renew, and are removed fairly when they no longer qualify Build pricing, billing, and provisioning that understands programs, including discounts, usage caps, credits, tax exemption, and self-serve purchase, so the next program is configuration rather than a project Build safe paths for organizations to move between their available plans and manage their teams, without losing data, seats, or history Work directly in partner teams' systems, such as billing, identity, and Safeguards Design for trust, with controls and audit trails that stand up to financial audit and student-privacy requirements Turn manual review, one-off fixes, and hand-run testing into tools that support, sales, and finance can use themselves Share on-call for program issues, and use what you see there to decide what to build next You might be a good fit if you: Have 6+ years of experience building software, with strong backend or full-stack skills and solid grounding in data modeling, APIs, and databases Have owned systems where mistakes are expensive, such as billing, payments, identity, entitlements, provisioning, or eligibility Have a track record of finishing work that depended on several teams, without formal authority over any of them Are comfortable in a large codebase you don't own, and learn the rules its owners care about Sweat correctness and edge cases, and can say clearly what you tested and what you didn't Enjoy unblocking people and closing things out, and leave the underlying system better each time Prioritize well when demand is larger than capacity, including saying no and explaining why Communicate clearly across engineering, finance, sales, and support, and care about the societal impacts of your work Strong candidates may also: Experience with subscription or usage-based billing, quote-to-cash, tax, or revenue systems, such as Stripe, Metronome, or Salesforce CPQ, or with building under SOX controls Experience with verification, KYC, fraud, or trust and safety systems Experience with enterprise identity and administration, such as SSO, SCIM, or large account and data migrations Experience building for schools, nonprofits, research institutions, healthcare, or government, or working with FERPA or similar privacy rules Experience launching in new countries, including currency, tax, language, and local eligibility Experience building products with large language models, or using coding agents heavily in your own engineering work Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Human Resource Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Human Resource Coordinator opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: Lisbon, Portugal About the Role: Do you thrive in a high performance role, solving complex problems and interacting with people? Are you passionate about helping customers and are a standout colleague? Cloudflare is seeking a Technical Support Engineer to join our team PAYGO. You will work with our customers on a variety of technical support issues as well as the Technical Operations team that is responsible for running our global distributed network. This is a position where you will learn the inner workings of Cloudflare's technology and gain a deeper understanding of internet technologies. You will provide support on our Application Performance and Developer Platform products. Examples of desirable skills, knowledge and experience: You thrive in a high performing team environment You take ownership and make sure you solve the customers issues. You drive the case to the finish line. You are familiar with Developer Platform products You have previous experience working as part of a team in a customer-facing role You have experience solving HTTP, DNS, SSL, Cache and other networking-related problems You understand how the Internet works You have a solid grasp of problem-solving with command line tools (curl/dig/traceroute/tcpdump) You have experience working in a support role. You are comfortable communicating through various support channels and always put the customer first (Emails, Live Chats, Phone calls and virtual meetings) You are a motivated self-starter and always looking to expand your existing skill set Bonus Points You are fluent in German, Japanese, French, Spanish, Portuguese or Mandarin You are familiar with Cloudflare and have a site actively using our platform You are familiar with Nginx, Apache, IIS or any other web servers You are committed to gaining a deeper understanding of the following technologies: DNS / CDN - Cache / SSL / Cloudflare Workers You have worked with PostgreSQL, MySQL, MS SQL or other database servers You have experience with Cloudflare Workers and/or JavaScript You have experience with Video encoding and streaming solutions Compensation Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location. We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet. Dear Pfizer Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate Manager - Investigation opportunity with Pfizer at Pfizer.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. Best,
Celina Lin

You will work across Compute Finance, Infrastructure Accounting, Capacity Planning, Fleet, Design & Construction, Operations, Procurement, Legal, Data, and Engineering. Strong hands-on proficiency in Python and SQL, with sound software-engineering and testing practices. Strong capability in at least one of classical ML, GenAI/RAG/ agents or MLOps /platform engineering, with working knowledge of adjacent areas. Good-to-Have Skills: Advanced ML and deep learning: Experience with PyTorch , TensorFlow, Hugging Face, scikit-learn, XGBoost , PyMC , computer vision, NLP, GNNs, causal inference or uncertainty estimation. Advanced GenAI and knowledge systems: Experience with LangChain , LangGraph , LlamaIndex , Semantic Kernel, AutoGen , CrewAI , hybrid retrieval, knowledge graphs, graph RAG or evidence verification. Cloud, data and MLOps : Experience with AWS, Bedrock or SageMaker, Databricks, Spark, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, MLflow , Airflow, Kubeflow or GitHub Actions. Agents and human-AI workflows: Familiarity with MCP-style integration, agent tracing, adversarial testing, durable workflows, permissions, human review, BI or process automation. Strong collaboration with business SMEs, product, architecture, software, data, platform, evaluation and control partners. Ownership, reliability and disciplined follow-through from design through production support. Ability to guide junior engineers and learn new tools through evidence-based experimentation. cold_email.subject: Interest in CDNA_Manager – Digital Analytics — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the CDNA_Manager – Digital Analytics opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Growth Merchant Lead - Emerging Markets (Grand Forks, ND)
jobs.description: About the Team The Emerging Markets team promotes growth in local economies by building meaningful partnerships with merchants across underdeveloped, high-opportunity markets. We focus on T4–T5 geographies—one of DoorDash’s highest company priorities, representing over 40% of remaining restaurant opportunities as we expand beyond core cities and suburbs. Our team creates first connections with SMB restaurants and retailers, helping them grow and monetize through on-demand delivery. This is a field sales opportunity with extensive travel within the region. You will need to live by or in proximity to a major airport. About the Role As a Growth Merchant Lead (GML) , you will play a pivotal role in expanding DoorDash’s footprint by opening new markets and bringing new restaurant partnerships onto the platform. You will own a high-velocity, in-person sales cycle and spend the majority of your time developing Tier 4-5 (“emerging”) markets – some of DoorDash’s largest remaining areas of opportunity. This role requires extensive travel (70%+) and is ideal for someone who is energized by building new markets from the ground up and influencing market growth directly. You’ll report to a Regional Sales Manager for the region and work cross-functionally with teams across the business. You’ll join a culture that prioritizes learning, ownership, and career development, with direct access to the support and resources you need to grow to the next level. This is a field sales role with extensive travel within the region. You will spend most of your time traveling in the region meeting with merchants, with some time working remotely. In addition, this role will require the ability to travel as needed for in-person collaboration through trainings, offsites, team-building events, and other business related necessity. You're excited about this opportunity because you will… Expand DoorDash’s presence by traveling to emerging markets and developing new restaurant partnerships. Lead end-to-end, in-person sales cycles– prospecting, pitching, negotiating, and closing. Sell business owners on DoorDash’s value and secure revenue-share agreements. Consistently execute high-volume field activity and close deals within days. Build scalable approaches and playbooks to accelerate market expansion. Shape DoorDash’s expansion strategy in rural economies. Have an outsized impact on growth in high-priority markets. We're excited about you because… You have 4+ years of in-person, outside B2B sales experience (field experience is required) You have proven success running short, high-velocity, full sales cycles – including same-day closes. You have strong prospecting, hunting, and negotiation skills. You are energized by extensive travel – spending 70%+ of your time in the field, including overnight travel inside and outside of your home state. You are entrepreneurial, adaptable, and motivated building and scaling new markets. jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (TPM, Compute)
jobs.description: Perplexity is looking for a technical program manager to own how we plan, bring online and run the GPU compute behind every product. Perplexity serves Ask, Computer and API traffic on GPU capacity across multiple cloud and neocloud providers, and demand shifts with every new customer, product launch and model release. Working across engineering, research, Finance and providers, you’ll forecast how much compute we need and when, bring new capacity into production, and own how the fleet performs today, driving fixes when reliability, utilization or cost fall short. The ideal candidate knows GPU fleets, handles technical and commercial details, and is energized by building a function with little precedent. OUR MISSION Perplexity’s mission is to power curiosity. Curious people are the people who drive change in the world. Driving change is a continuous cycle of learning, building, and integrating. Learn: curious people constantly learn new things by asking more. They question the status quo in their own expertise and they constantly learn outside of it. Research is essential to them and never ending. Build: curious people make and create things, to show the world their new answers to problems no one else ever questioned. They take action on what they’ve learned. Makers need tools to create their products, their companies, their reality. Integrate: they must interact with the world as it is to drive change and adoption. True leaders do not simply build something and hope. They must have armies of agents and workers who can constantly work in millions of small ways. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Partner with Finance on the compute demand forecast, 3–12 months out, driven by customer growth, model releases, and post-training and evaluation plans rather than trend lines - Turn the forecast into decisions with Finance and engineering leadership on commitments and budget, checking that new capacity fits the plan before we commit - Bring new capacity online and lead transitions, from contract to production, including provider onboarding, acceptance criteria, migration and decommissioning - Build a single, trusted view of the fleet: capacity, cost, allocation, and uptime, reliability and utilization by provider and workload - Drive daily utilization, reliability and cost-efficiency as core metrics, reclaiming idle capacity and surfacing trade-offs rather than letting them become side effects - Own inference and compute requests end to end: triage and resolve GPU, deployment and quota requests from teams across Perplexity, and build self-serve paths so routine requests no longer need a person in the loop - Manage compute provider relationships, with scorecards and regular reviews of reliability, support and delivery, and use that data to shape how we work with providers over time - Partner with engineering, research, and finance teams on capacity decisions that match the different needs of training, batch inference and real-time production inference - Build the operating system for compute: the processes and tooling to request, plan, allocate and track compute, with clear owners QUALIFICATIONS - 6+ years of technical program management, capacity planning or infrastructure operations in cloud environments, leading programs across teams and vendors - Direct experience with GPU or accelerator fleets across training and inference workloads - Experience working directly with cloud or neocloud providers on reserved capacity, capacity commitments, onboarding or vendor performance management - Experience with infrastructure cost modeling, unit economics or cost attribution in partnership with Finance - Technical depth in cluster management, scheduling and orchestration, and the data skills to build forecasts and dashboards yourself - The judgment to surface hard trade-offs and communicate them clearly from engineers to executives - Thrives in a small, agile team; has initiative and desire for ownership without much precedent to lean on

jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Bristol Myers Squibb Netherlands Bristol Myers Squibb has been active in the Dutch market for over 50 years, employing people across a range of activities and business units in Utrecht, The Netherlands. The Netherlands is also home to our first European Cell Therapy facility, located at the Leiden Bio Science Park, the largest life sciences cluster of The Netherlands. This new state of the art facility is focused on commercial manufacturing with capabilities for multi-product Cell Therapy manufacturing. You can become part of this exciting journey. Check out this video if you want to know more about it! The Netherlands has everything it takes to become the medicines hub of Europe, the so-called Boston by the North Sea. As we continue to expand our footprint by building this new site, we are looking to grow our team. Would you like to become an important chain in our worldwide network to bring this new personalized treatment to patients suffering from blood cancer? Join us and be a game changer! For more information about Bristol Myers Squibb Netherlands, visit us at bms.com/nl or careers.bms.com/nl Position Summary Leiden Cell Therapy Site is seeking a dynamic individual to join a team of materials management and supply chain professionals. This individual is responsible for executing routine activities related to the management, cleansing, and movement of all types of materials (e.g., cold chain and ambient) supporting internal and external customers while following Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Key Responsibilitie s Ensure routine activities such as receipt, storage, transfer, distribution, disposal, and cleaning of all types of materials (ambient, cold chain, dangerous goods, etc.) are performed according to GMP procedures. Prepare all types of materials for shipment to internal and external parties in accordance with GMP procedures. Ensure materials are appropriately labeled in accordance with written GMP procedures. Perform inventory control practices, including cycle counting and rejected/expired material disposition, as described in GMP procedures. Write procedures to maintain a safe and organized working environment. Perform inspection of incoming materials to the work area according to procedures. Use material handling equipment (gas-powered, electric, and/or manual) in accordance with procedures. Handle materials based on material specifications, including temperature-controlled, dangerous, or hazardous materials, according to procedures. Assist in setting up operational equipment and fixtures, and support facility and equipment commissioning activities as requested. Respond to system and equipment alarms during and outside office hours as part of a rotating schedule, in accordance with GMP procedures. Facilitate ambient and cold chain sampling in collaboration with employees from other departments. Review GMP documentation and perform data verification. Coordinate internal and external customer requests across multiple unit operations during assigned shifts, including personnel, materials, and logistical requirements. A biotechnology pioneer since 1980, Amgen has grown to be one of the world’s leading independent biotechnology companies, has reached millions of patients around the world, and is developing a pipeline of medicines with breakaway potential. Observational Research is an increasingly important component in drug development and commercialization. There is increased demand for information from Real-World Data (RWD) studies for regulatory and reimbursement authorities. The Center for Observational Research (CfOR) at Amgen partners with teams to generate real world evidence for multiple stakeholders across the product lifecycle. CfOR studies include but are not limited to evidence generation regarding the frequency and distribution of disease, the clinical burden of disease, the natural history or clinical course of disease, the design of clinical trials, treatment cost and utilization patterns, and the safety and effectiveness of therapeutic interventions. ​ Amgen is seeking an Epidemiology Analyst (RWD researcher) to join our CfOR organization based in Hyderabad, India . In this role, the individual will contribute to research activities in the Data and Analytics Center (DAC) on functionally aligned teams. The ideal candidate should have strong knowledge of observational research methodology, excellent communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work across various therapeutic areas and regions. The Epidemiology Analyst is recognized as a strong scientific contributor and is a first or contributing author for papers in peer-reviewed journals, abstracts for scientific congresses or for internal reports that enhance the company’s mission. Key Activities include: o Contribute to global observational research activities for CfOR in support of drug development, registration, and commercialization across Amgen’s portfolio of products o Skills & Qualifications • 5-9 over all experience with Bachelor's or Master’s degree in the relevant Engineering field. • Exposure to single-use systems, biotechnology, or pharmaceutical manufacturing is preferred. • Confident with accurate data entry and organizing information in engineering databases or similar systems. • Detail-oriented, reliable, and able to manage assigned work independently. • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work collaboratively with engineers and cross-functional partners. • Motivated to learn, ask questions, and contribute to a supportive team environment. Key Competencies • Engineering Fundamentals – Applies core engineering concepts to understand single-use system information and recognize when clarification or review is needed. • Data Quality and Organization – Enters and organizes technical information accurately and consistently so that it can be used by a broad engineering community. • Independent Execution – Plans and completes defined assignments with care, follows through on open items, and seeks guidance when needed. • Communication and Collaboration – Builds productive working relationships across sites and functions and communicates questions and status clearly. • Learning Agility – Develops knowledge of new systems, engineering practices, and Amgen operations through training, research, and engagement with subject matter experts. Role Focus This role combines independent database and engineering support work with opportunities to collaborate across nearly all Amgen sites and a range of functions. The Engineer will develop focused expertise in a new single-use systems area and gain exposure to how engineering, manufacturing, process development, and supply chain work together. .
